meta.name: State fiscal notes and third-party analyses

provenance.source: Kansas Division of the Budget (KDOR estimate, Feb 20, 2026)

rows.notes: The fiscal note scores the same provisions PE modeled (standard deduction to $3,805/$8,640/$6,480 from TY2026, same baseline). Its fiscal-year mapping (FY2027 = 100% TY2026 + 30% TY2027) implies about -$10.6M for TY2026 vs PE's -$8.88M — a 16% smaller magnitude, plausibly because KDOR simulates actual Kansas returns (capturing all standard-deduction claimants) while PE uses survey-based microdata. The FY2026 column is zero and FY2027 stacks 130% of a tax year, so per-tax-year figures are the right comparison.

provenance.source: GA Dept. of Audits & Accounts / OPB, Fiscal Research Center (revised note, Feb 24, 2026)

rows.notes: The fiscal note scores the full 0.20pp cut (5.19%->4.99%) from a 5.19% baseline; its individual-income-tax impacts are -$840M (FY2027, inflated by refunds of over-withholding) and -$680M (FY2028, first normalized year), which bracket PE's -$800.6M. At validation time policyengine-us encoded GA at 5.09% for 2026 (per the HB 1437 schedule as accelerated by HB 1015 and HB 111), so PE natively saw a 0.10pp cut and the analysis scaled to model the full cut. Note the premise is now historical: HB 1001 died in the Senate and the 4.99% rate was enacted via HB 463; policyengine-us master now encodes 4.99% for 2026.
Verified verbatim: $36.73M net 2027, $71.51M gross standalone, $265,965 phase-out, dependent-exemption swap.

conditions.bill_title: Utah HB210 S2: Marriage Penalty Removal

provenance.source: Utah Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst (2nd Sub. HB210, 2026-02-05)

rows.notes: The LFA scored 2nd Sub. HB210 (the version PE modeled), and the steady-state sign agrees: both score it revenue-raising ongoing, because halving single/HOH phase-out thresholds outweighs the new ~$158 joint-filer credit (~113,000 taxpayers pay ~$161 more vs ~125,000 paying ~$150 less, per the note). Magnitude diverges sharply: PE's +$11.48M is ~9x the LFA's ongoing +$1.29M/yr - and if compared to the LFA's first year (FY2027 nets -$299,400 due to a one-time item), even the sign differs. PE likely over-scores the threshold-halving pickup or under-scores the credit. Caveat: the House voted down (31-42, Mar 2 2026) the later S05 version, which phases thresholds in from 2030.

conditions.bill_title: CT SB78: SS Benefit Deduction Threshold Elimination

provenance.source: Connecticut OFA score of sSB-1 Sec. 6, committee version (identical policy; struck by Senate Amendment A before passage - not enacted)

rows.notes: No OFA note exists for SB78 itself; the identical policy (full SS deduction for all filers) appeared as Sec. 6 of the Finance committee's sSB-1 (File 692), which OFA scored at -$57.5M (General Fund, FY28, capturing tax year 2027). PE's TY2026 -$56.1M is within 2.4% - and since OFA notes the loss grows annually with beneficiaries, a slightly smaller TY2026 figure is expected. Consistent with OFA's Tax Expenditure Report ($223M/yr for the existing deduction; this bill adds only the remaining 25% for above-threshold filers). Caveat: Senate Amendment A replaced sSB-1 with the budget implementer before passage, so this is a score-vs-score comparison against a proposed, unenacted version; the $75K/$100K thresholds remain current law.
